<small>'''Glasgow Name Study:''' [[Space:Glasgow Name Study|main page]] · [[Space:Glasgow Research|research directory]] · [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] · [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan]]</small>

== Research question and current position ==

The records show a substantial McCaughan-name presence around Lisnagaver, Gortereagh, Church Tamlaght, Gortahar, Ballydonnelly and Rasharkin. The spellings overlap, but the evidence does not yet prove one common family. This page therefore separates known WikiTree clusters from unattached documentary occurrences and keeps the evidence for each group distinct.

'''Main unresolved question:''' can [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]], wife of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]], be connected to one of these documented households? Her Rasharkin baptism records identify her as Mary McAughin/Molly McAughern, but do not name her parents.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms">Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, published transcription of PRONI MIC1P/292, entries 75, 106 and 203: [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Baptisms, 1834 sequence].</ref>

'''Current best hypothesis:''' Mary came from the '''Gortereghy McCaheran group''', with '''James McCaheran''' the leading named candidate for her father. The nearest WikiTree comparison is [[McCaughan-68|James McCaughan]] (before 1790, Antrim), but the profile is not identified with the 1834 Gortereghy tenant. The case is geographic and chronological: William and James McCaheran were Gortereghy co-tenants in 1834, and Mary and Alexander's first located child was baptised from Gortereagh in 1837. Confidence remains low because no relationship-bearing record has yet linked Mary to James, William or any other McCaheran household.

'''Working rule:''' no parent should be added to Mary's WikiTree profile until a marriage, baptism, lease, probate, witness record or equivalent source supplies a direct bridge.

=== What is not proved ===

* No parentage for [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]] has been proved.
* [[McAughin-2|Archibald McAughin/McCaheren]] is a known WikiTree research cluster, but the current profile cannot yet be safely mapped to both 1851 Archibald households; his fatherhood of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]] is not proved.
* The older 1851 Archibald household, including Mary age 22, is not proved to be the same man as the Archibald whose children were baptised to Elisabeth Kilpatrick.
* The graveyard memorial's Robert McCaughin has not yet been formally identified with [[McAughin-4|Robert McAughin]], although the relationship and timing make it a high-priority comparison.
* [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]]'s marriage to [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]] connects to [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]]'s family, not automatically to [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]].
* The unidentified 1875 Mary Anne M‘Caughern witness is not identified with Alexander's wife.
* No common ancestor is established for all the spelling variants on this page.

=== Local cluster index ===

This is the page's working navigation map. A question mark marks an estimated or disputed date; a proposed WikiTree relationship is not counted as proved.

'''Descendant-count conventions:''' “WikiTree-linked” means the current family fields; “record-confirmed” means a relationship found in a census, baptism, marriage, probate or memorial; “not audited” means the available evidence is insufficient for a reliable total.

The Rasharkin baptism register adds a potentially important link around this collateral branch. It records '''Jane Glascaw''', born 29 April 1846, as daughter of '''Thos Glascaw''' and '''Mary Ann McCrackin''' at '''Lisnagaver'''. It also records several children of '''James Dysart and Jane Glascaw''' in Granagh and Crushybracken. Because [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[McCracken-5681|Maryann (McCracken) Glasgow]] are independently documented at Lisnagaver, Jane is a strong but not yet proven candidate for their daughter. If the identification is confirmed, the John McCaughern–Sarah Dysart line is affinally linked to the Thomas Glasgow family through Jane, not directly to [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]].<ref name="GlascawDysartNetwork">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription], entries 82, 133, 176, 192, 203, 269 and 271.</ref>

'''Assessment:''' this strengthens the local Glasgow–Dysart–McCaughern network, but does not prove that Sarah Dysart was Jane's sister or that [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]] belonged to either family. Sarah's own baptism and the original 1851 marriage certificate remain decisive.

=== Record-level Dysart–McCaughan marriage evidence ===

FamilySearch's indexed civil-registration entry records '''John McCaughan''' marrying '''Sarah Dysart''' at Rasharkin on 18 March 1851. The associated persons identify '''Jas McCaughan''' as John's father and '''Jas Dysart''' as Sarah's father. The image is unavailable, so the original certificate still needs to be checked for residences, occupations and witnesses. This is now documented marriage/parent-name evidence, not merely a public-tree reconstruction.<ref name="FSDysartMcCaughan">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGVD-CN3S FamilySearch civil record], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

Griffith's Valuation (1861–62) lists '''James Dysart''' and '''Robert Dysart''' at '''Crushybracken''', and '''Archibald Dysart''' and '''Sarah Dysert''' at '''Drumack'''. This confirms a concentrated Dysart presence in the same Rasharkin parish, but it does not prove that the Sarah Dysert entry was the 1851 bride or that these households were one family.<ref name="RasharkinDysartValuation">[https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-rasharkin.php Griffith's Valuation, Rasharkin parish], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

'''What this does not prove:''' Jas McCaughan is not yet identified with the Gortereghy tithe tenant; Sarah Dysart is not shown to be Jane Glascaw's sister; and this collateral branch does not establish the parents of [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]].

=== Local-family testimony ===

In a 17 May 2008 Bann Valley genealogy-list reply, a writer identifying himself as '''Robert McCaughern''' said that he still farmed at Ballydonnelly and that “all the McCaugherns around Rasharkin were related.” He also mentioned a Rea farm formerly adjoining his family’s farm. This is useful local testimony and makes the Rea clue in the John McCaughern–Sarah Dysart reconstruction worth testing, but it is not a historical record and cannot assign [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]] to a particular McCaughan branch.<ref name="LocalMcCaughernTestimony">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/archive/BannValley/2008/msg00074.html Bann Valley archive: Rea], 17 May 2008; [https://genealogy.torrens.org/archive/BannValley/2008/msg00068.html related Ballydonnelly message], 16 May 2008.</ref>

=== John–Mary Gormley branch confirmed in the census-search-form index ===

The National Archives of Ireland census-search-form database identifies '''Thomas McCaughern or McCaughan''' of '''Church Tamlaght, Gortahar, Rasharkin''' in the 1851 extract, with father '''John McCaughern''' and mother '''Mary Gormley'''. This independently confirms a parent-bearing McCaughern branch in the same local area. It is not evidence that this John was related to [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]; the chronology makes this branch a poor fit for her circa-1811 parentage unless the current dates are substantially wrong.<ref name="NAIThomasMcCaughern">[https://censussearchforms.nationalarchives.ie/search/cs/results.jsp?applicantAddress=&amp;applicantFirstname=&amp;applicantSurname=&amp;barony=&amp;censusExtractYear=&amp;city=&amp;county=&amp;fatherFirstname=&amp;fatherSurname=&amp;motherFirstname=&amp;motherSurname=&amp;pageSize=10&amp;pager.offset=56160&amp;parish=&amp;search=Search&amp;sort=residence_parishSort&amp;townland= National Archives census-search-form index], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

=== Mary McCaughan date discrepancy ===

The current WikiTree+ suggestions report lists [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow (McCaughan)]] with a '''certain 1817 birth at Lisnagaver''', while the research case has generally used about 1811 from the 1851 census age. The same report flags an expired source reminder, so 1817 is a current tree assertion rather than verified evidence. Recovering that source is now a priority because it could materially change the chronology of candidate parents.<ref name="Mary1817Assertion">[https://plus.wikitree.com/Profiles/Suggestions/IRL_ANT/981_Hidden_0.htm WikiTree+ Antrim suggestions report], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

== Core evidence: Mary McCaughan and the Gortereagh/Lisnagaver network ==

=== Alexander Glasgow × Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow ===

Rasharkin Presbyterian records preserve the following forms:

* [[Glasgow-3939|James Glasgow]], born 17 January 1837 and baptised 9 February 1837, son of Alex Glascaw and Mary McAughin of Gortereagh;
* [[Glasgow-3940|Unnamed Glasgow child]], an incomplete 1838 entry naming Alex and Molly McAughern of Gortereagh; and
* [[Glasgow-973|James Glasgow]], born 9 October 1843 and baptised 7 January 1844, son of Alex and Molly McAughern of Lisnagaver.<ref name="RasharkinBaptisms2">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription], entries 75, 106 and 203.</ref>

The 1851 household also supports the couple's identity and includes [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-438|Ann (Glasgow) McCracken]] and the younger James. Other children in the maintained reconstruction include [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Glasgow Elder]].<ref name="AlexanderHousehold">1851 Lisnagaver household for Alexander and Mary Glasgow; public search route through the [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/ National Archives of Ireland census collection].</ref>

The 1834 tithe transcription lists William and James McCaheran at Gortereagh and Archy McCaheran near Lisnagaver.<ref name="Tithe1834">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionorder.pdf North Antrim tithe revision/order transcription], Rasharkin entries, 1834.</ref> This makes the McCaheran locality relevant to Mary's investigation, but does not identify any of those men as her father.

An earlier Protestant-householders return lists '''John McCaughan''' in Kilconway, Rasharkin, together with a widow under the recorded form '''McCaghan'''. This establishes that the McCaughan/McCaghan spelling family was present in the Rasharkin barony by 1740, but gives no townland, age, spouse or descendants and cannot be connected to any later profile without an intermediate record.<ref name="Householders1740">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740religiousreturnsulstername.pdf Protestant Householders' Returns (1740)], entries 2008 and 2009 for Kilconway, Rasharkin.</ref>

'''Assessment:''' couple and children documented by church/census evidence; Mary's parentage remains open.

=== The Alexander Glasgow neighbourhood in 1851 ===

The local entries around [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]'s Lisnagavor house 35 are more useful than the distant county-wide surname hits:

* house 31: the older Archibald McCaheren household, with Elizabeth and five children;
* house 35: Alexander and Mary Glasgow with Robert, James and Ann;
* house 13: John and Margaret Taylor with Mary McCaheren, age 70, recorded as Margaret's mother;
* house 17: Daniel Montgomery's household with John McCaughern, age 11, a weaver's apprentice;
* house 1: the younger Archibald McCaheren household, including Robert, John, Elizabeth and Hugh;
* house 4: William McCaheren's household, including Alexander, Andrew, Mary Jane, Elizabeth, Sarah and nephew Charles;
* house 5: Sarah McCaghrin with grandson Daniel and granddaughters Sarah and Margaret; and
* Moneyleck: Hugh McCahen, wife Mary and children Jane, Wilson and Catherine, alongside widower John McCahon and his daughter Margaret.

This neighbourhood map shows that Alexander's family sat among several distinct McCaheren/McCaughern/McCahen/McCahon households and a McCaheren woman embedded in the Taylor family. It strengthens the local network case but gives no direct parentage for [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]].

=== Competing James McCaughern burial candidate ===

The authenticated FamilySearch index and the linked Find a Grave memorial identify a '''James McCaughern''' born about 1790 and buried at Rasharkin Presbyterian Church Graveyard after his death on 13 September 1858. The memorial associates him with '''Nancy McCaughern''' (about 1794–1859) and child '''Thomas McCaughern''' (about 1829–1857).<ref name="JamesBurial1858">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:CVDP-S2MM FamilySearch burial index: James McCaughern], and [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/205517378/james-mccaughern Find a Grave memorial 205517378], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

This is a substantial local comparison candidate because the estimated birth year fits an adult tenant in the 1834 Gortereghy tithe and the Presbyterian/Rasharkin setting fits the wider network. It is '''not''' yet the same man: the memorial does not state Gortereghy, William McCaheran, Mary Glasgow or any parentage, and the spouse/child relationships are contributor data rather than an inspected original record. It is also distinct from the younger James McCaheren, age 20, in the 1851 Lisnagaver household; that younger James is the one tentatively matched by the new Ancestry tree to Archibald and Elizabeth Kilpatrick.

'''Assessment:''' the 1790–1858 James/Nancy memorial is now the best local burial candidate for the unidentified older James, but it remains unproved as the Gortereghy tithe tenant and has no demonstrated connection to [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]. The next tests are the grave photograph/inscription, James's marriage or probate, and any Rasharkin/Kilraughts church record naming his residence or children.

=== The two Archibald McCaheren households ===

The 1851 return contains two separate Archibald McCaheren households. The current [[McAughin-2]] profile appears to map most closely to the younger household, but the WikiTree family structure may currently combine people from both.

==== Younger Archibald and Elizabeth Kilpatrick ====

'''Born:''' about 1805? — inferred from the 1851 return's death entry; the WikiTree profile currently gives about 1791.<br/>
'''Died:''' in spring 1851, reported age 46.<br/>
'''Wife:''' [[Kilpatrick-3058|Elizabeth Kilpatrick]] (about 1803–about 19 January 1881).<br/>
'''Locality:''' Lisnagaver, Rasharkin.

The current WikiTree structure gives Archibald and Elizabeth six children, including [[McAughin-1|Mary Jane (McAughin) Elder]], [[McAughin-3|Catherin McAughin]], [[McAughin-4|Robert McAughin]], [[McAughin-5|John McAughin]], [[McAughin-6|Elizabeth McAughin]] and [[McAughin-7|Hugh McAughin]]. The 1851 household and baptism evidence instead place John, Elizabeth and Hugh in a younger Archibald household and do not list Mary Jane. The current profile structure may therefore combine the two 1851 Archibald families and needs review.<ref name="ArchibaldProfile">[https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/McAughin-2 WikiTree: Archibald (McAughin) McCaheren], descendant view and profile data, accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

The 1851 Lisnagaver census contains two separate Archibald McCaheren households. The older Archibald, age 60, died in the return and had Elizabeth age 58 and children including Mary age 22. The younger Archibald, age 46, also died in the return and had Elizabeth age 48 with children Margaret, Catherine, Robert, John, Elizabeth and Hugh. The age, household composition and baptism sequence distinguish them.<ref name="Census1851">1851 Census of Ireland, Rasharkin district, Lisnagaver households; public search route through the [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/ National Archives of Ireland census collection].</ref>

The Rasharkin baptism transcription adds direct child records to the younger household: '''John McAughern''', born 5 April 1838 and baptised 4 July 1838; '''Elisabeth McAughern''', born 9 April 1842 and baptised 19 May 1842; and '''Hugh McAughern''', born 10 April 1845 and baptised 7 June 1846. All three are recorded as children of Archy and Elisabeth Kilpatrick at Lisnagaver. Their ages match the children in the age-46 household, not the older Archibald household containing Mary.<ref name="ArchyBaptisms">Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, entries 109, 155 and 267: [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html published transcription of PRONI MIC1P/292].</ref> This is stronger than the profile structure alone and confirms the McAughern spelling in the younger Archibald–Elizabeth household. It does not connect either Archibald to [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]].

'''Assessment:''' younger Archibald–Elizabeth Kilpatrick household is supported by three direct baptisms and the 1851 age-46 household. The current [[McAughin-2]] profile and proposed [[McAughin-1|Mary Jane]] relationship require reconciliation against the separate older Archibald household.

==== New lead: James McCaughern, born about 1831 ====

Ancestry's public-name index now returns a user-tree reconstruction for '''James McCaughern''' (1831–8 May 1900), born in Rasharkin. It gives his parents as '''Archibald McCaughern/McCaheron/McCochrane''' (1791–1881) and [[Kilpatrick-3058|Elizabeth Kilpatrick]] (1803–1881), and says James married Ann McCord and had four children. The same index lists a son James (1859–1931), a daughter Margaret (1856–1860), Ann McCord and Jane McCaughern (1858–).<ref name="AncestryJames1831">[https://www.ancestry.it/genealogy/records/james-mccaughern-24-6fzfwm Ancestry public-name index: James McCaughern (1831–1900)], accessed 14 September 2026. User-tree material is derivative and must be checked against the underlying 1851 census, civil marriages, deaths and original baptism records.</ref>

This is a significant new clue because James's estimated birth year matches the '''James McCaheren, age 20''' in the older 1851 Lisnagaver household, while the cited Archibald birth estimate (about 1791) matches that household's Archibald, age 60. It therefore strengthens the working identification of the 1851 James as a son of the older Archibald household. It does '''not''' prove that this James was the 1834 Gortereghy tithe tenant, the father of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]], or the same person as [[McCaughan-68|James McCaughan]].

'''Research status:''' high-value derivative lead; medium chronological fit; no direct parentage proof. The next check is the underlying 1851 image and James's 1850s–1870s marriage/death records, especially for residence, father's name and the Ann McCord/Jane Caldwell relationships.

=== Other 1851 Lisnagaver households ===

The 1851 return should be treated as several households, not one extended family:

=== New FamilySearch Rasharkin search results ===

The authenticated FamilySearch record search adds several local entries that were not previously used in the argument. A civil-registration result for a '''John McCaughan''' marriage at '''Rasharkin on 18 March 1851''' names '''Jas McCaughan''' as his father and Sarah Dysart as his spouse. The record does not give enough information here to identify either John or James with the Glasgow-connected families, but it is a genuine father-naming result from the correct district and should be checked against the original certificate and later household records.<ref name="FSJohn1851">[https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/record/results?count=100&amp;q.anyPlace=Rasharkin&amp;q.surname=McCaughan FamilySearch Rasharkin McCaughan search], accessed 14 September 2026; the result is the 18 March 1851 Rasharkin marriage of John McCaughan and Sarah Dysart, with father Jas McCaughan.</ref>

The same search returned '''Archibald Mccaughan Junr''' in a '''1836 Lisnagaver''' Valuation Office Books entry. “Junr” is significant because it indicates a second Archibald in the locality, consistent with the two-Archibald problem already visible in the 1851 return. It is not yet safe to identify this valuation entry with [[McAughin-2|Archibald McAughin]], his father, or the younger/older household without inspecting the image and neighbouring entries.<ref name="FSArchibald1836">[https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/record/results?count=100&amp;q.anyPlace=Rasharkin&amp;q.surname=McCaughan FamilySearch Rasharkin McCaughan search], accessed 14 September 2026; 1836 Lisnagaver Valuation Office Books result for Archibald Mccaughan Junr.</ref>

The wider authenticated search also returned '''Archey McCaheran''' and '''John McCaheran''' in the Northern Ireland Tithe Applotment Books, 1822–1840. The FamilySearch index does not expose the townland or assessment details in the result summary, so these should be treated as discovery leads to compare against the full North Antrim tithe transcription, where the 1834 Gortereghy co-tenants are already recorded. They are not automatically additional people or proof of a relationship.<ref name="FSTitheMcCaheran">[https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/record/results?count=100&amp;q.anyPlace=Rasharkin&amp;q.surname=McCaheran FamilySearch McCaheran search], accessed 14 September 2026; Northern Ireland Tithe Applotment Books, 1822–1840 results for Archey and John McCaheran.</ref>

'''Assessment:''' the new results strengthen the case for reconstructing multiple McCaughan/McCaheran families in the Rasharkin–Lisnagaver area and add one independent father-naming lead. They do not identify [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]]'s parents. The original images and full townland entries remain necessary before these men can be placed into a family cluster.

An independent public Geneanet tree reproduces the John McCaughern–Sarah Dysart marriage and proposes a death for John on 18 December 1872 and a daughter, Mary Anne Jane Rea McCaughern, born about 1858 at Crushybracken. This is useful for following the branch into later records, but it is still user-submitted derivative material, not independent proof. It should be used to locate the original death, daughter’s birth/marriage and any migration record—not to identify John or Jas McCaughan with [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s family.<ref name="GeneanetDysart">[https://pt.geneanet.org/fonds/individus/?go=1&amp;niveaux_1___3869569569__=arbres&amp;niveaux_2___3645179592__=arbres%23utilisateur&amp;nom=MCCAUGHERN&amp;sourcename__0__=bobspree Geneanet public McCaughern tree index], accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

'''Assessment:''' multiple same-locality households are precisely why spelling and proximity cannot be used as parentage proof.

=== Best current hypothesis for Mary McCaughan's parentage ===

The strongest working hypothesis is that [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan/McAughin]] came from the '''Gortereghy McCaheran group''', particularly '''James McCaheran'''. The 1834 tithe return lists William and James McCaheran together at Gortereghy, and Mary's first located child was baptised from Gortereagh in 1837 shortly after the couple's reported 1836 marriage. This is a local-origin hypothesis, not proof.

The alternatives are Archy McCaheran at Lisnagaver and John McCaheran at Moneyleck, both also recorded in the 1834 Rasharkin tithe return. The two 1851 Archibald households do not contain a Mary of the right age to be Alexander's wife, so the older household's Mary age 22 must not be used as evidence for [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]. The younger Archibald–Elizabeth Kilpatrick household is a later child-bearing household and is chronologically incompatible as Mary's parental household.

'''Current assessment:''' James McCaheran of Gortereghy is the leading named candidate for Mary's father, at low confidence. No parent should be added to her WikiTree profile until a marriage, baptism, lease, probate or witness record supplies a direct bridge.<ref name="GortereghyMcCaheranTithe">[https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionorder.pdf 1834 North Antrim tithe return], Rasharkin entries 7490, 7496 and 7521; compare [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism], entry 75.</ref>

'''Additional local lead:''' the 1851 Taylor household includes Mary McCaheren, age 70, as Margaret Taylor's mother. This may eventually identify a maternal sibling network, but no record yet connects Margaret Taylor to Alexander's wife. An Ancestry-derived John McCaughern family at Lisnagaver is also a comparison lead, not proof. Do not promote either lead above James McCaheran without original relationship-bearing records.

== Other local McCaughan / McAughern families and associates ==

=== John McCaughern, Jane McAuley and the Ballydonnelly children ===

[[McCaughern-15|John McCaughern]] (about 1813–1901) is shown on WikiTree as the husband of Jane (McAuley) McCochrane and father of [[McCaughern-9|Alexander (McCaughern) Cochrane]]. Alexander's profile gives his father as John McCaughern, teacher, and documents Alexander's 1876 marriage in Tamlaght and 1878 marriage at Finvoy. The profiles place this family in the Ballydonnelly/Rasharkin–Finvoy area.

This family deserves separate treatment because the published Rasharkin baptism transcription also records a '''James McAughern''', born 22 May 1843 at Ballydonnelly, son of '''John and Jane McAuley'''. The matching parents and locality make James a plausible additional child of the John-and-Jane household, but the WikiTree profile does not currently list him and the transcription spelling is McAughern. This is a promising bridge, not a proved identification until the original baptism and the family's household records are compared.

'''Assessment:''' coherent local WikiTree family; Alexander's father-naming evidence is strong; James's placement in the same family is probable but not yet proved. This cluster is distinct from the Archibald–Elizabeth Kilpatrick household unless a record links the two.

=== James Mc Caughern and Rose Mooney ===

[[Mc_Caughern-19|James Mc Caughern]] (1824–1889), born and deceased at Ballydonnelly, is shown as the husband of Rose (Mooney) Mc Caughern and father of [[Mc_Caughern-10|Mary (Mc Caughern) Mc Mullan]]. The profile currently has only an Ancestry family-tree source and no parents. It is therefore a real Ballydonnelly family group, but it cannot yet be joined to the John–Jane McAuley family or the older Gortereghy James.

'''Assessment:''' local household cluster, low documentary confidence; keep separate pending original civil/church records.

=== William McCaughern and Elizabeth Taylor ===

[[McCaughern-5|William McCaughern]] (about 1825–1916) is shown as son of Charles McCaughern and Louisa M. Gaussen, husband of Elizabeth Taylor and father of Charles McCaughern. The profile places the marriage in County Londonderry about 1845 and William's death at Rasharkin in 1916. This is a County Londonderry/Rasharkin line, but its parent links and source quality are not yet sufficient to connect it to the Gortereghy tenants.

'''Assessment:''' separate WikiTree family-field line with limited source detail; useful comparison family, not currently part of the Alexander–Mary or Archibald clusters.

=== Moneyleck McCahon–Wilson family ===

[[McCahon-44|Joseph McCahon]] (1867–1941) is described in the profile biography as the son of '''Hugh McCahon''' and '''Mary Jane Wilson'''; the profile's structured parent fields remain unknown. He was husband of Hannah Wilson and father of Hugh, Robert Wilson, Margaret Anne, Enos Archibald and Mary Jane Wilson McCahon. His 1893 marriage and the 1901/1911 census summaries place the household at '''Moneyleck, Rasharkin'''. The marriage witnesses included Hugh Wilson, identified in the profile as Joseph's cousin. This is a later and well-localised McCahon/McCaughan-variant branch, but no record currently connects Hugh or Mary Jane to the older Gortereghy James or to Mary Glasgow.

'''Assessment:''' strong later Moneyleck household evidence; retain as a separate Rasharkin branch and investigate its parent generation independently.

=== WikiTree-linked Hugh McCaughan comparison cluster ===

[[McCaughan-4|Hugh McCaughan]] (about 1824–about 1903) is shown as the son of [[McCaughan-5|Hugh McCaughan Sr.]] (estimated about 1806) and [[McCurdy-193|Roseanne McCurdy]], and brother of [[McCaughan-7|Archibald McCaughan]] (about 1799–about 1870) and [[McCaughan-6|Elizabeth McCaughan]]. His wife was [[Erwin-428|Mary Erwin]]; listed children include [[McCaughan-16|Mary]], [[McCaughan-17|Alexander]], [[McCaughan-18|Hugh Jr.]] and [[McCaughan-19|Archibald]]. The family is a useful WikiTree-linked comparison branch, but the dates are internally strained and no profile evidence places it in Rasharkin, Lisnagaver or Gortereghy. It must not be merged with the Alexander–Mary family.

The later Moneyleck family includes [[McCahon-44|Joseph McCahon]] (1867–1941), whose profile names Hugh McCahon and Mary Jane Wilson as parents, [[Wilson-71886|Hannah Wilson]] as wife, and [[McCahon-18|Enos Archibald McCahon]] as a son. The profile links FamilySearch person [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MCJX-HRD MCJX-HRD]. This confirms a local later McCahon branch, not Mary's parentage.

The account's later '''James McCaughan''' (born about 1792, son of John born about 1754) must be kept separate from [[McCaughan-68|James McCaughan]], whose WikiTree profile gives birth before 1790, wife [[Larny-2|Mary Larny]] and son [[McCaughan-67|John]] (about 1798). The current dates make the two identifications incompatible; the Ballyverdagh James is not a safe candidate for the Canadian John line or for Mary's father.

=== 1669 Hearth Money Rolls: earliest direct North Antrim occurrences ===

The [https://adamsfamilydna.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/1669-Hearth-Money-Rolls-for-North-and-Mid-Antrim.pdf 1669 Hearth Money Rolls] list '''Ogan McCaghan''' at Kilcroagh, Armoy; '''Allex McCahan''' and '''John McCaghan''' at Ballyverdagh, Culfeightrin; '''Angus McCahir''' at Cross Denard, Culfeightrin; '''Gillindrish McCagher''' at Loughan/Ballyloghan, Culfeightrin; and '''Daniell McKaghin''' in Dunluce town. The standardized index treats these as McCaughan entries, while the historical spellings vary.

These are the earliest direct household-head records currently in the catalogue and establish a substantial McCaughan-name presence in the wider Culfeightrin–Armoy region before the 1740 Rasharkin returns. They provide no ages, spouses or children and no bridge to Lisnagaver, so they are regional ancestral candidates and surname-network context only. None can presently be assigned as a parent of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]].

=== Directly recorded McAughern sub-branches ===

The Rasharkin register separates several parent couples that should not be collapsed into the Archy–Elisabeth Kilpatrick family:

These entries are important because they show the spelling family across several nearby townlands and several unrelated or presently unlinked parent couples. None currently provides a relationship to [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]].<ref name="SubbranchBaptisms">Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription, entries 163, 192, 218, 228, 234 and 249: [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html published transcription of PRONI MIC1P/292].</ref>

=== Thomas McCaughern / John McCaughern / Mary Gormley lead ===

The National Archives of Ireland search-form results include a 1851 request for '''Thomas McCaughern or McCaughan''' at Church Tamlaght, Gortahar, Rasharkin, giving father '''John McCaughern''' and mother '''Mary Gormley'''. This is an index/search-form result, not the original census extract.<ref name="ThomasSearchForm">National Archives of Ireland, [https://censussearchforms.nationalarchives.ie/search/cs/results.jsp?applicantAddress=&applicantFirstname=&applicantSurname=&barony=&censusExtractYear=&city=&county=&fatherFirstname=&fatherSurname=&motherFirstname=&motherSurname=&pageSize=10&pager.offset=56160&parish=&search=Search&sort=residence_parishSort&townland= 1851 census search-form results], Thomas McCaughern or McCaughan entry.</ref>

'''New associated lead:''' Ancestry's public-name index also returns '''Mary McCaughern''' (about 1835), born in Rasharkin Parish, with the same reported parents, '''John McCaughern/McCarnagh''' (about 1809–1867) and '''Mary Gormley/Gorman/German''' (about 1813–1894). It reports her marriage to William Marks and seven children, including Nancy, Mary Ann, Robert, Elizabeth, James, Nancy and Samuel Marks.<ref name="AncestryMary1835">[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/genealogy/records/mary-mccaughern-24-5ldvs9 Ancestry public-name index: Mary McCaughern (about 1835)], accessed 14 September 2026. User-tree material is derivative and no WikiTree profile has yet been identified for this Mary.</ref>

This does not identify Mary McCaughan Glasgow, who was born about 1811, but it materially strengthens the existence of a separate John–Mary Gormley McCaughern family in the Rasharkin area. It also provides a possible sibling/household route for the 1851 Thomas search-form entry. The parent and child relationships remain unproved until the underlying civil, church or census records are inspected.

'''Assessment:''' promising collateral family lead; no WikiTree IDs safely assigned yet; original extract and identity must be obtained before linking it to any other cluster.

=== Andrew McGaughern of Church Tamlaght ===

A Rasharkin Church of Ireland graveyard transcription records Andrew McGaughern of Church Tamlaght, who died 11 July 1909 aged 68. The memorial names siblings James, Margaret Ann and William, wife Hannah, son Andrew and later descendants.<ref name="RasharkinGraves">[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinCOI/graveyard.html Rasharkin Church of Ireland graveyard inscriptions], McGaughern/McCaughin entries.</ref>

No WikiTree IDs have been assigned here because the memorial has not yet been tied to an individual profile. This is a later Church Tamlaght family cluster to compare with the 1851 Thomas/John/Mary Gormley lead, not evidence that either belongs to Alexander's wife's family.

=== Robert McCaughen × Nancy Glasgow ===

WikiTree currently connects [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]] as spouse of [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]], daughter of [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[McCracken-5681|Maryann (McCracken) Glasgow]]. Nancy was born about 1848 in the Rasharkin area and is shown as marrying Robert McCaughen in the Ballymoney registration district in 1879.<ref name="NancyProfile">[https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1362 WikiTree: Nancy Glasgow], including the current spouse and parent links; see also [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/McCaughen-4 WikiTree: Robert McCaughen].</ref>

This is an important McCaughen–Glasgow connection because it is a named marriage link, not merely a shared townland. It belongs to the [[Glasgow-987|Thomas Glasgow]] family, however, and must not be silently merged with [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]'s family. A copy of the original 1879 marriage registration, including fathers, residences and witnesses, would determine how much genealogical weight the link deserves.

'''Assessment:''' WikiTree marriage connection to a Glasgow family; original marriage evidence still required; no present proof that Robert was related to [[McAughin-2|Archibald McCaheren]] or to [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]].

=== McCaughern–Elder probate and directory network ===

==== Daniel M'Caughern of Ballydonnelly ====

A RootsChat discussion quotes a PRONI probate-calendar entry for '''Daniel M'Caughern of Ballydonnelly''', who died 12 January 1893. The quotation names '''John Elder of Lisnagaver''' and Samuel M'Caughern. The underlying calendar or will remains uninspected, so the quoted relationship wording cannot yet be used as proof.<ref name="DanielProbate">[https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=502783.0 RootsChat discussion quoting the 1893 PRONI probate entry]. Secondary quotation only.</ref>

==== John Elder and Robert M'Caughern ====

The National Archives of Ireland calendar for John Elder, who died 30 January 1904 in County Antrim, names Robert M'Caughern as secondary executor/beneficiary.<ref name="Elder1904">National Archives of Ireland, [https://www.willcalendars.nationalarchives.ie/search/cwa/details.jsp?id=1639459843 will-calendar entry for John Elder].</ref> The 1910 directory lists Robert M'Caughern, farmer, at Lisnagava and John Elder as Rasharkin postmaster; the 1943 directory again lists Robert McCaughern, farmer, at Lisnagaver.<ref name="Directories">[https://www.libraryireland.com/UlsterDirectory1910/Rasharkin.php 1910 Ulster Directory, Rasharkin] and [https://www.lennonwylie.co.uk/PT194314.htm 1943 Belfast and Ulster directory transcription].</ref>

'''Assessment:''' genuine Elder–McCaughern documentary network; identities and kinship between the named people remain to be resolved.

=== Mary Anne M‘Caughern witness in the John Glasgow family ===

On 18 February 1875 at Finvoy Parish Church, [[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]], daughter of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]], married Francis Bellingham. The witnesses were Thomas Bellingham and '''Mary Anne M‘Caughern'''.<ref name="Bellingham1875">[https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/McCaughan-222#_note-BellinghamGlasgow1875 WikiTree source note for the 1875 Bellingham–Glasgow marriage].</ref>

This is a useful record-level link between John's Glasgow family and a McCaughern surname form. The witness is unidentified and must not be equated with [[McCaughan-222|Mary/Molly Glasgow]]: the record says Mary Anne, uses M‘Caughern, and does not establish that Alexander's wife was living in 1875. It is a network observation, not proof that [[Glasgow-867|John]] and [[Glasgow-951|Alexander]] were related.

== Wider comparison material ==

=== Pre-1790 North Antrim records ===

The earliest located records establish that the surname and its variants were already present across the north Antrim area before the later Rasharkin families:

* '''1740, Rasharkin/Kilconway:''' the Protestant Householders' Returns list '''John McCaughan''' under the spelling '''McCaghan''', plus a separate widow under the same surname. This is the earliest directly located Rasharkin occurrence, but the return gives no age, townland, spouse or children, so it cannot yet be connected to Mary or James.<ref name="McCaghan1740">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf Protestant Householders' Returns (1740)], Kilconway barony, Rasharkin entries 2406–2407.</ref>
* '''1740, wider north Antrim:''' additional McCaughan/McCaghan forms occur at Ballintoy, Derrykeighan, Ramoan, Ballywillan and Loughguile. These show a broad regional footprint rather than a single Rasharkin-only family.<ref name="McCaughan1740Wider">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf Protestant Householders' Returns (1740)], surname-sorted entries for McCaughan/McCaghan.</ref>
* '''1766, Ballymoney parish:''' Elizabeth was recorded as '''m'Caghna''' in the Religious Census for Ballymoney parish. No household relationship or age survives in the published surname-sorted extract.<ref name="McCaghna1766">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1766census/1766religiouscensusballymoney.pdf 1766 Religious Census for Ballymoney parish], PRONI T808/15264, record 145.</ref>
* '''1755, Ballymoney Presbyterian register:''' a published extract of the old Ballymoney Presbyterian baptism book records Agnes, daughter of James McCaughan, on 20 May 1755, and Janet, daughter of Alexander McCaughan, on 28 August 1755. These are explicit parent-child records in the nearby Presbyterian network, but neither father is identified with the later Rasharkin family.<ref name="BallymoneyBaptisms1755">[https://electricscotland.com/webclans/m/maceachain2.htm Compiled North Antrim McCaughan account], quoting the Ballymoney Presbyterian Church Old Sessions Baptismal Book, entries dated 20 May and 28 August 1755; original register should be checked.</ref>
* '''1734–1775, Culfeightrin/Ballyverdagh tradition:''' a compiled account identifies Laughlin McCaughan (born about 1696 at Ballyverdagh) and records the form '''Laughy McCagen/McCahan''' in a 1734 County Antrim surname roll. It says his will was proved in 1772 and that he was buried at Culfeightrin. The account also reports earlier John, Charles and Alexander McCaughan generations and later parish-vestry forms such as McKachan and McKaghin. This is a valuable lead to test against the original roll, will and vestry minutes, but it is not proof that the Culfeightrin line connects to the Rasharkin McCaheran households.<ref name="BallyverdaghMcCaughan">[https://electricscotland.com/webclans/m/maceachain2.htm Clan MacEachain, Ballyverdagh/Culfeightrin McCaughan account], compiled secondary narrative, accessed 14 September 2026.</ref>

'''Implication:''' pre-1790 evidence now confirms a regional McCaughan/McCaghan presence and supplies a potentially traceable Culfeightrin family with a 1772 probate trail. It does '''not''' yet provide a named parent for [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]] or identify the 1834 Gortereghy James as a descendant of any early household.

=== 1803 North Antrim surname footprint ===

The 1803 agricultural census adds an earlier, wider North Antrim surname footprint. It records '''Robert McCaghin''' at Ballynagard Upper, '''Archibald McCaghin''' at Ballyvarridagh, '''Archibald McCaughin''' and '''Alexander McCaughin''' at Farranmacarter, and a household at '''Coulrasheskin''' headed by a McCaghan family with sons '''John''' and '''Archibald''', all in or near the barony of Culfeightrin/Ballintoy. These are valuable locality and spelling records, but they are not the Rasharkin Lisnagaver households unless an intermediate record is found. In particular, the Farranmacarter and Coulrasheskin entries may represent separate branches and must not be merged with the later Alexander Glasgow household merely because the given names recur.

Source: [1803 Agricultural Census for parts of North Antrim](https://www.billmacafee.com/1803agriculturalcensus/1803censusantrim2.pdf), records 3843, 3909, 4144 and 4157.

The 1831 North Antrim tithe transcription shows the later continuity of this wider Culfeightrin group: John junior, Laughy and John at Ballyvennaght/Ballyverdagh; John at Coolaveely; Daniel and Laughy at Brackney; John at Eglish; and Patrick and Alexander at Farranmacarter. This is a dense McCahan cluster in the Ballycastle/Culfeightrin area, but it remains geographically separate from Rasharkin's Gortereghy McCaheran entries and supplies no direct bridge to Mary Glasgow.<ref name="CulfeightrinTithe1831">[https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrim.pdf North Antrim tithe transcription], 1831 Culfeightrin entries for McCahan/McCaughan.</ref>

The same census yields ten additional record-only findings which broaden the comparison set without proving relationships:

# '''Armoy:''' Archibald and Hector McCauhan are listed together at Armoy.
# '''Bunshanacloney:''' Loghy McCaughan is recorded separately in Armoy barony.
# '''Stroan:''' Neal McCauhan is another Armoy-barony occurrence.
# '''Tureagh:''' Daniel McCauhan is recorded in the same barony.
# '''Broughgammon:''' John McKaghon appears in Ballintoy barony.
# '''Craig:''' Angus McKaghan appears in Ballintoy barony.
# '''Currysheskin:''' James, Archibald, Archibald Junior and Isaac McKaghan form a named local cluster.
# '''Drumnagee:''' Duncan senior, Duncan junior and John McKaghan form another named cluster.
# '''Drumnagessan:''' John McKaghon is recorded separately from the Drumnagee group.
# '''Kilmahamogue:''' Charles McKaghan is recorded in Ballintoy barony.

These ten findings show that the 1803 surname footprint is geographically broad and includes repeated Archibald, John, Daniel, Angus and Duncan names. None should be attached to a later WikiTree profile without marriage, baptism, land or other linking evidence.

The wider 1851 census extraction adds 100 record-level McCaugh/McGaugh/McAugh variant entries across Antrim. The full catalogue is retained in the Glasgow-951 research findings working notes; it includes Dunaghy, Glenleslie, Legagrane, Tullynewey, Killyglen, Larne, Lisnagavor, Moneyleck and other localities. These entries expand the comparison population but do not by themselves join the households.

=== Hector McCaughin and Mary Hill ===

The WikiTree family fields identify Hector McCaughin (born about 1805 in Antrim) as husband of Mary Hill and father of [[McCaughin-11|Margaret]], [[McCaughin-12|Alexander]], [[McCaughin-13|Daniel]], [[McCaughin-16|Grace]] and [[McCaughin-2|Patrick]]. Hector's profile in turn identifies [[McCaughin-10|Alexander McCaughin]] (estimated about 1780) as his father. US census entries and an obituary support Hector's later New York household and the children's sibling structure, but the parent assignment to the older Alexander is not independently sourced on the inspected profiles. Several children later emigrated to New York and Vermont. This is therefore a WikiTree-connected variant group, not a proved Irish-origin lineage or Rasharkin branch.

'''Assessment:''' most fully connected McCaughin group found in the WikiTree audit, but the Irish parent assignment is only as strong as the unsourced WikiTree family fields and it is not connected to Rasharkin's Gortereghy/Lisnagaver families.

The wider McCaughan index below is intentionally not forced into the North Antrim clusters. Similar spelling and geography alone do not establish descent.

=== WikiTree spelling-variant audit ===

On 14 September 2026, WikiTree's person search was run for the surname forms below, using birth dates approximately 1750–1900 and birth-location keyword '''Ireland'''. The results are an inventory of profiles, not a claim that the people share a family. County Antrim, County Londonderry, County Down and other Irish results are retained because the surname network crosses those borders. Profiles already described in the family clusters above are repeated here only when needed to make the audit complete.

* '''McCaughen:''' no Ireland-born profiles appeared in the date/location-filtered search. [[McCaughen-4|Robert McCaughen]] remains catalogued separately because his WikiTree birth is in New Zealand and his marriage links him to [[Glasgow-1362|Nancy Glasgow]].
* '''McAughin:''' [[McAughin-2|Archibald (McAughin) McCaheren]], [[McAughin-1|Mary Jane (McAughin) Elder]], [[McAughin-3|Catherin McAughin]], [[McAughin-4|Robert McAughin]], [[McAughin-5|John McAughin]], [[McAughin-6|Elizabeth McAughin]] and [[McAughin-7|Hugh McAughin]]. ==== WikiTree's related surname-variant results ====

WikiTree's search interface itself maps several further forms to this surname family. These are catalogued as comparison profiles only; the spelling map is not evidence of a common ancestor.

'''Audit conclusion:''' the profiles above are now catalogued as either local WikiTree-linked clusters or unassigned comparison profiles. The searches do not prove that WikiTree's surname-variant algorithm represents one biological family, and they do not identify Mary's parents. Exact searches returned no WikiTree profiles under several historically attested record spellings, so the absence of a profile is not evidence that no historical person existed.

Source: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Special:SearchPerson WikiTree Person Search], surname searches for the forms listed above, filtered to birth dates approximately 1750–1900 and birth-location keyword Ireland, accessed 14 September 2026.

=== FamilySearch identity collision: Scottish and Rasharkin Alexanders ===

The authenticated FamilySearch Tree profile [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/G8WJ-HFW G8WJ-HFW] is internally conflated. Its source list contains Irish records for the Rasharkin Alexander, but its family panel also attaches a Scottish wife, Mary McCaughan (MQ57-B2Y), Scottish children and a Barony, Lanarkshire marriage. The archived discussion on [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] identifies the Scottish marriage as Alexander Glasgow and Mary Fleming on 12 June 1838 in Barony, Lanarkshire, with an 1841 Barony household headed by a flesher.

That Scottish couple is distinct from the Rasharkin farmer: his son James was baptized at Gortereagh on 9 February 1837, before the Scottish marriage, and he appears with Mary and children at Lisnagaver in 1851. The Mary Fleming marriage therefore does not disprove [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan]] as Alexander's wife. It is a significant identity correction, but it does not identify Mary's parents. The FamilySearch tree should be treated as a conflated derivative tree until the two Alexanders are separated.

Sources: [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/G8WJ-HFW FamilySearch G8WJ-HFW], [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/sources/G8WJ-HFW source list], [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/MQ57-B2Y FamilySearch MQ57-B2Y], and [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-951#comments archived WikiTree discussion], accessed 14 September 2026.

=== Ballymena death-index candidate: Mary M'caughren, 1894 ===

FamilySearch contains an exact-ish local civil index entry for '''Mary M'caughren''': death registration in '''Ballymena, County Antrim''', October–December '''1894''', page 69, volume 1. The index gives age '''81''' and estimated birth year '''1813'''. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FTZ5-6ZJ FamilySearch civil-registration index entry]

The age and county make this a worthwhile identity lead, but it cannot presently be identified with [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]]. The index has no residence, spouse, informant, townland, parents or associated persons; the image is unavailable; and it post-dates the current 27 February 1892 death for Mary Glasgow. It therefore does not justify changing Mary's death date or adding parents. The next test is to obtain the underlying civil death certificate through the General Register Office/IrishGenealogy route, if available, and check the residence and informant.

=== 1803 Ballintoy household census ===

A separate 1803 household return for Ballintoy parish records two structured McCaughan households at '''Coulrasheskin/Curryeshkin'''. House 3 contains '''Archd. M'Caghan''', wife '''Isobel Lawson''', sons Archd. and John, and brother Alex, a weaver. House 4 contains '''Arch. senior M'Caghan''', wife '''Sarah Linegan''', son Isaac, daughters Sally, Giles and Ibby, and brother Robert. [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1803traillcensus.pdf Robert Traill's 1803 Ballintoy household census transcription], PRONI T679/69, p. 27, entries 1417–1427.

This is direct household evidence for a multi-generational North Antrim network and helps separate the Ballintoy/Culfeightrin cluster from the Rasharkin Gortereghy hypothesis. Neither household contains a Mary of the right apparent age; the younger Archibald would also be too young to be [[McAughin-2|Archibald McAughin]], estimated born about 1791. It does not identify Mary's parents.

The same compiled Ballyverdagh/Culfeightrin account gives a secondary pedigree lead: John McCaughan (about 1724–1793), husband of Agnes McCahan, with children John (about 1754), Alexander (1756), Archibald (1758), Sarah (1760), Mary (1761) and Charles (1763). It says John was served heir to his father in 1771. The listed Mary McCaughan is only a chronological possibility for a mother of an about-1811 child, and no evidence connects her to Rasharkin; the original heir, will and parish records remain to be checked.

=== FamilySearch Rasharkin/Ballydonnelly branch ===

FamilySearch links '''James Mcaughern''' (22 May 1842–13 December 1896, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/GWCJ-8BK GWCJ-8BK]) to '''John McCaughern''' (about 1813–1901, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/LCRH-Z1G LCRH-Z1G]) and '''Elizabeth Hansen''' (about 1813–1843, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/LCRH-DL2 LCRH-DL2]), married Rasharkin in 1834. Their listed children include '''John McCaughern''' (1835–1907, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/MZQT-2TK MZQT-2TK]) and James. The 1842 James was born at Ballydonnelly and christened at Rasharkin.

The same Tree connects '''James Mcaughern''' (1830–1900, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/949C-MM6 949C-MM6]) to '''James McCaughern''' (about 1790–1858, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/L11Q-5KR L11Q-5KR]) and '''Nancy Marks''' (about 1794–1859, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/L119-DTP L119-DTP]). The younger James married '''Mary Jamison''' ([https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/KLP6-P27 KLP6-P27]) at Finvoy on 9 March 1854 and had '''James Mcaughern''' (1868–, [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/949C-MMM 949C-MMM]).

This is a distinct local branch, not proof of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow's]] parentage. The about-1790 James could be chronologically possible for a daughter born about 1811, but the displayed children are Daniel (1826), Thomas (1829), James (1830) and William (1842), with no Mary; the 1830 James is too young. The original 1834 marriage, 1842 baptism and records for the older James's children remain the priority checks.

=== FamilySearch civil-marriage proof for the older James's children ===

The authenticated FamilySearch source list for [[https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/L11Q-5KR|James McCaughern]] (about 1790–1858) contains two relationship-bearing indexed marriage records. The 27 November 1850 civil marriage of Daniel McAughern and Eleanor Graham records Daniel as age 24, estimated birth about 1826, and explicitly names '''James Mc Aughern as his father'''; the original place is Churchtown, Ballymoney. [[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FGXX-H6G|FamilySearch record FGXX-H6G]]

The 9 March 1854 marriage of James McCaughern and Mary Jamison at Finvoy likewise explicitly names '''James McCaughern as the groom's father'''. [[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FG6V-QGF|FamilySearch record FG6V-QGF]]

These records materially strengthen the identification of the 1790–1858 James/Nancy household and document two sons, Daniel and James. They do not prove that this James was the 1834 Gortereghy tithe tenant or the father of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]: neither record names Mary, Glasgow, William McCaheran or Gortereghy.

=== Pre-1790 Rasharkin McCaharan graveyard root ===

The [[https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinCOI/graveyard.html|Rasharkin Church of Ireland graveyard transcription]] records '''Andrew McCaharan''', who died '''1 February 1738 aged 69''', and separately names his son '''John McCaharan''' on the same memorial. This is a direct local memorial and places the McCaharan spelling in Rasharkin more than a century before [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s estimated birth.

It is a new root cluster for the surname study, but not a proved ancestor line: the transcription gives no John's wife, townland, full death information or intervening generations. It strengthens the case for a long-established local surname population while leaving Mary's parentage unproved. The original stone image or burial/register material should be sought to recover the remainder of John's inscription.

=== 1740–1796 Tamlaght O'Crilly / Drumcannon McCaughan continuity lead ===

The [https://adamsfamilydna.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/1740-Protestant-Returns-Londonderry-County-Ireland.pdf 1740 Protestant Householders' Returns] identify '''John McCahan''' and '''James McCahan''' in '''Tamlaght O'Crilly''', Loughinsholin barony. This is an unusually early, exact-parish occurrence of two McCaughan-variant householders, decades before the Rasharkin baptismal material. The return gives no ages, household composition or relationship between the two men.<ref name="Evidence1740TamlaghtMcCahan">1740 Protestant Householders' Returns, records 1171–1172.</ref>

A later [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/misc/rentrolls.html circa-1800 Bann Valley rent-roll transcription] records four McCaughan tenants in '''Drumcannon''' in '''1791''': '''Samuel''', '''Matthew''', '''William''' and '''John'''. The dated entries are a landlord record, not a census. The [https://www.billmacafee.com/1796flaxgrowerslist/1796flaxgrowersderry.pdf 1796 Flaxgrowers' List] then records '''William M'Caughin''' in '''Tamlaght O'Crilly''' with three wheels/looms.<ref name="Evidence1791Rent1796Flax">Drumcannon entries 182, 185, 197–198; 1796 Flaxgrowers' List, record 4754.</ref>

This is new pre-1811 evidence in the same broader parish region and strengthens the case for investigating Tamlaght O'Crilly, Drumcannon and Gortereghy together. It does not prove the parents of [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]: the named tenants have no demonstrated relationship to her, and the 1791 William has not been shown to be the 1796 William. The next test is to trace these names through surviving estate papers, Presbyterian records and valuation revisions for a daughter Mary born about 1811 or a transfer into Lisnagaver/Gortereghy.

=== New full 1803 Ballintoy McCaughan household audit ===

The complete [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1803traillcensus.pdf 1803 Ballintoy agricultural census] reveals several distinct early McCaughan households beyond the previously isolated Coulrasheskin entries:

* '''Broughgammon:''' deceased Dennis M'Caghan; widow Margaret McCurdy; John, Molly, Betty, Nancy and Matty.
* '''Drumnagessan/Cairn-Hill:''' John M'Caghan and Sarah McCaw; sons David, Archibald, John and James; daughter Isobel.
* '''Drumnagessan:''' Daniel M'Caghan and Rose McCurdy; daughters Catherine, Sally and Isobel.
* '''Templastragh:''' Daniel M'Caghan and Rose McCurdy; sons John, Alexander, Roger and Robert; daughter Mary.
* '''Templastragh:''' Hector M'Caghan and Peggy Laverty; son Zachariah and daughter Rose.
* '''Templastragh:''' John M'Caghan and Jane Sinclair; sons Hector and Daniel.
* '''Craige:''' Angus M'Caghan and Elizabeth Glass; sons Hugh and Archibald; daughter Belle.

The two Daniel-and-Rose entries occur as separate census households in different townlands and must not be merged without proof. The Templastragh Mary is directly recorded as a daughter of Daniel M'Caghan and Rose McCurdy, but no age, later marriage, migration or Rasharkin connection is supplied. This confirms a substantial early, multi-branch Ballintoy network, but none of these households can presently be assigned as the parents of [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]]. Targeted WikiTree searches found no matching profiles for these exact household combinations, so no IDs are invented here.

=== 1824 Templastragh tithe continuity ===

The later [https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionnamespdf.pdf North Antrim tithe revision] independently preserves the Templastragh cluster: it lists '''Zackariah McCahan''', '''Daniel McCahan''', '''Alexander McCahan''' and a '''widow McCahan''' there in 1824. Zackariah is especially notable because the 1803 Ballintoy census names '''Zachariah McCaghan''' as the son of '''Hector McCaghan''' and '''Peggy Laverty'''. Daniel and Alexander also recur as names in the 1803 Daniel-and-Rose household, although the tithe does not state their relationships or ages.<ref name="Evidence1824TemplastraghContinuity">[https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionnamespdf.pdf North Antrim tithe revision names], records 800–801 and 807–814.</ref>

This is genuine chronological corroboration for a continuing McCaughan/McCahan presence in the same Ballintoy townland, and it helps distinguish the early Templastragh households from isolated name occurrences. It still cannot identify the 1803 Mary as the later [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]]: the tithe gives no women’s identities beyond the widow, no marriages or children, and no movement toward Lisnagaver or Gortereghy.

=== 1766–1860 Templastragh locality trail ===

The 1766 [https://www.billmacafee.com/1766census/1766religiouscensusballintoy.pdf Religious Census for Ballintoy] records '''Daniel M'Kaughen''' in '''Templastragh''', with a household size of five. This is a direct pre-1790 occurrence of the same distinctive given name and townland later seen in the 1803 census. The 1803 household is much larger—Daniel M'Caghan, Rose McCurdy and five listed children, including Mary—and the 1824 tithe revision again lists Daniel McCahan in Templastragh.<ref name="Evidence1766TemplastraghDaniel">[https://www.billmacafee.com/1766census/1766religiouscensusballintoy.pdf 1766 Ballintoy Religious Census], record 348.</ref>

The later [https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-ballintoy.php Griffith's Valuation index] also lists '''Daniel McCahan''' and '''Elizabeth McCaughan''' in Templastragh. Because the valuation is a later occupier index and does not state ages, spouses or parentage, this may represent a younger Daniel or a different household; it cannot be assumed to be the 1803 man. Taken together, the records establish a long-lived Daniel/McCaughan presence in Templastragh from 1766 through the mid-nineteenth century and justify targeted searches for a marriage or baptismal record connecting the households.

This materially strengthens the Ballintoy cluster but still does not prove that the 1803 Mary was [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]] or that Daniel and Rose were her parents.

=== Later Daniel-and-Elizabeth Templastragh branch ===

An [https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/jane-mccaughan-24-1mzn0 Ancestry public-name index] identifies '''Jane McCaughan''', born '''12 November 1834''' at '''Templastragh''', as daughter of '''Daniel McCaughan''' and '''Elizabeth Rogers'''; the same compiled entry estimates both parents at about 1800–1847 and says Jane later emigrated to New York. This is a useful later-household lead because Griffith's Valuation also lists Daniel McCahan and Elizabeth McCaughan in Templastragh.

The index is derivative and does not expose the original baptism or marriage images. It therefore cannot yet establish whether this Daniel was a son of the 1803 Daniel and Rose, a nephew, or an unrelated Daniel in the same townland. It does, however, give a specific child, date, mother’s maiden surname and migration trail for further testing. No evidence currently connects this branch to [[McCaughan-222|Mary (McCaughan) Glasgow]].

=== First Kilraughts register: confirmed archival target ===

The [https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/accessions/2002/02digests/religion.htm National Archives catalogue] confirms that '''First Kilraughts Presbyterian Church''' records survive at PRONI as '''MIC/1P/462''', including registers and minute books from '''1815–1984'''. An independent [https://ulsterlees.azurewebsites.net/families/co-antrim/ballymoney-area/ North Antrim reconstruction] identifies a marriage in that register on '''8 November 1839''' and gives witnesses, confirming that the register preserves marriage-level detail. The couple's reported 1836 marriage should therefore be searched in the same register under Glasgow/Glasgo/Glassgow and every McCaughan/McAughin/McAughern/McCaughren variant.

This is the clearest remaining route to a contemporaneous record associated with Alexander and Mary. It may name witnesses rather than parents, so even a successful marriage entry may not prove Mary's parentage; however, repeated witnesses could connect her to one of the local McCaughan households. The register must be consulted directly before any conclusion is upgraded.

=== Collateral Drumadarragh McCaughey branch ===

The [https://ulsterlees.azurewebsites.net/families/co-antrim/ballymoney-area/ Ulster Lees reconstruction] documents a separate '''John McCaughey/McCaghy and Margaret Lees''' family associated with '''Drumadarragh''', including Jane (about 1812), Margaret (about 1825), James (about 1833), Sarah (about 1835) and other proposed children. Several adult marriages name John McCaghy as father, and Jane's later death record names John McAughley and Margaret Lees. This branch is geographically relevant to the Ballymoney-area McCaughan variants and explains why the 1817 Drumard household cannot be treated as the only local candidate.

The published reconstruction does not include a daughter Mary of the correct age and remains partly inferential. It is therefore a comparison/exclusion branch, not evidence that John and Margaret were Mary's parents.

=== 1817 First Ballymoney McCaughan household: a new Mary-parent candidate ===

Rev. Robert Park's 1817 register of the First Ballymoney Presbyterian Church records '''John McCaughan [McCahon]''', wife '''Mary McCaughan [McCahon]''', and son '''James McCaughan [McCahon]''' at '''Drumard [Drumart]''', house 8. The same register records '''Grissel McCaughan [McCahan]''' and '''Hugh McCaughan [McCahan]''' in a Bendooragh household.<ref name="Evidence1817BallymoneyMcCaughan">[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1817parkcensus.pdf 1817 First Ballymoney Presbyterian register], records 2912–2914 and 570–571.</ref>

A separate compiled Ballyverdagh account lists a Drumant church-member household as John and Mary McCahon, with son James and daughters Mary and Elizabeth. That detail is not present in the searchable Park register entry and the underlying membership source has not been inspected, so it remains a secondary lead. If the records refer to the same couple, their daughter Mary would be chronologically compatible with [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s estimated birth about 1811; no marriage, migration, residence or Glasgow connection has been found.

This is a chronological candidate, not proof of Mary's parents. The decisive test is the original Drumard/Drumant membership sheet and the couple's later Ballymoney Presbyterian, valuation and civil records. [https://electricscotland.com/webclans/m/maceachain2.htm Compiled Ballyverdagh account].

=== Complete 1817 Ballymoney-area McCaughan audit ===

The full searchable 1817 register contains at least five distinct McCaughan/McCahon placements: '''Charles and Elizabeth McCaughan''' at Balnamore, with children James, Samuel, John, Ann, Daniel and Elizabeth and an older Mary whose relationship is uncertain; '''Samuel and Martha McCaughan''' at Taghey, with sons John and James; '''John and Mary McCaughan''' at Drumard, with son James; '''Grissel McCaughan''' and '''Hugh McCaughan''' in a Bendooragh household headed by William McMaster; and '''Elizabeth McCaughan''' in a Currysiskan household headed by Widow Knox.<ref name="Evidence1817CompleteMcCaughanAudit">[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1817parkcensus.pdf complete searchable 1817 register], records 1239–1248, 1383, 1436–1439, 2912–2914 and 570–571.</ref>

The primary searchable register does '''not''' list a daughter Mary in the Drumard John-and-Mary household. The separate compiled account's Drumant list of daughters Mary and Elizabeth may represent a different membership list or townland, so it cannot currently prove that the Drumard couple had a daughter Mary. The Balnamore Mary is also uncertain and may have been Charles's mother. None of these placements supplies a marriage, parent statement, migration record or Glasgow link. Mary Glasgow's parents remain unproved.

=== Dreen probate cluster: Agnes and Peter McCaughern, 1916 ===

The [[https://www.willcalendars.nationalarchives.ie/reels/cwa/005014919/005014919_00647.pdf|National Archives of Ireland will-calendar]] records two adjacent Dreen, Rasharkin estates: '''Agnes McCaughern''', spinster, died 26 March 1916, administration granted to '''William McCaughern'''; and '''Peter McCaughern''', farmer, died 27 February 1916, also granted to William. Later unadministered grants for both estates were made to '''Catherine McCaughern''', spinster.

These entries show a substantial late local McCaughern cluster and a repeated William–Catherine administrative connection, but the calendar does not identify their exact kinship. The underlying probate packets should be obtained because they may name beneficiaries, relatives and property. This is a useful local-network lead, not evidence for [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow's]] parents.

=== New parent-bearing Armoy/Cromaghs branch: William McCaughan ===

The National Archives of Ireland census-search-form index gives a new parent-bearing local record: '''William McCaughan''', whose present address was Fairhill Street, Ballycastle, supplied an 1851 census extract naming his father '''Archibald McCaughan''' and mother '''Mary'''. The indexed residence was '''Cromaghs, parish of Armoy, barony of Cary''', placing this branch in the wider Ballycastle–Armoy area rather than directly at Lisnagaver or Gortereghy.

This proves an additional Archibald–Mary McCaughan parental pair in the wider North Antrim research region, but it does not identify William with any existing WikiTree profile or connect him to [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]. The record is a census-search-form abstraction rather than the underlying 1851 return, and the next step is to obtain the extract/image and trace William, Archibald and Mary through Cromaghs valuation and church records. No safe WikiTree ID has been assigned to this branch.

Source: [[https://censussearchforms.nationalarchives.ie/search/cs/results.jsp?applicantAddress=&applicantFirstname=&applicantSurname=&barony=&censusExtractYear=&city=&county=&fatherFirstname=&fatherSurname=&motherFirstname=&motherSurname=&pageSize=&pager.offset=14290&parish=&search=Search&sort=residence_baronySort&townland=|National Archives of Ireland census-search-form index]], accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Cromaghs valuation corroboration: Archibald and Margaret McCahan ===

Two independent online transcriptions of Griffith's Valuation for Armoy, dated to the 1861/62 county survey, list '''Archibald Mc Cahan''' as an occupier in '''Cromaghs'''. The same entries also list '''Margaret Mc Cahan''' in Cromaghs. This corroborates the parent-bearing 1851 census-search-form branch: the Archibald named there was an Archibald of the same surname variant and townland in the next decade.

The entries do not state whether Margaret was Archibald's wife, sister, daughter or another household occupier. The valuation is an occupier/property record, not a family register. The spelling is '''McCahan''', while the 1851 search-form entry uses '''McCaughan'''; this is compatible with local spelling variation but cannot identify either person with [[McCaughan-222|Mary Glasgow]]'s family. No safe WikiTree ID has been found for Archibald or Margaret.

Sources: [[https://irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-armoy.php|Irish Genealogy Hub transcription of Armoy Griffith's Valuation]]; [[https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/armoy.php|Fáilte Romhat transcription]]; [[https://nationalarchives.ie/help-with-research/research-guides/valuation-office-records/|National Archives guide to valuation records]]. Accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Pre-1790 Ballintoy record: Archd. McKaughin at Lisbellanagroagh More ===

The 1766 Religious Census for Ballintoy parish records '''Archd. McKaughin''' at '''Lisbellanagroagh More''', identified as Protestant. This is a new pre-1790 occurrence of the McCaughan spelling family in the barony of Cary, the same wider North Antrim barony containing later Ballintoy, Armoy and Ballycastle McCaughan/McCahan households.

The census supplies no age, household composition or relationship to Mary Glasgow. It cannot identify this Archibald as her father, and Lisbellanagroagh More is not the same place as Lisnagaver/Gortereghy. It is nevertheless a valuable locality and spelling lead for testing whether the later Armoy/Cromaghs and Rasharkin branches descend from an older Cary family.

Source: [[https://www.billmacafee.com/1766census/1766religiouscensusballintoy.pdf|1766 Religious Census for Ballintoy parish]], entry 318, accessed 15 September 2026.

=== Lisbellanagroagh continuity: Catherine M'Caghan and Daniel McCaw ===

The 1803 Ballintoy census records '''Kath. M'Caghan''', standardised as Catherine McCaughan, at '''Lisbellanagroagh Beg'''. She was listed as the wife of John McIlfatrick and as Church of Ireland; the row gives her age as 29, implying an estimated birth about 1774. The 1824 Ballintoy tithe book then records '''Danl. McCaw''' at '''Lisbellanagroagh More''', the neighbouring “More” townland where the 1766 census had recorded Archd. McKaughin.

These records create a continuous locality trail from an Archibald in 1766, to a McCaughan woman in the adjoining townland in 1803, to a McCaw occupier in More in 1824. They do not prove that Catherine was Archibald's daughter, that Daniel was related to either person, or that this Cary cluster was the family of [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan Glasgow]]. They are nevertheless stronger than isolated surname occurrences and justify targeted searches of Ballintoy Church of Ireland marriages, baptisms and vestry records.

Sources: [[https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1803traillcensus.pdf|1803 Trail census, Ballintoy]], entries 2852–2853; [[https://www.billmacafee.com/ballintoy/earlydatabases/titheballintoy.pdf|1824 Ballintoy tithe applotment]], entry for Daniel McCaw at Lisbellanagroagh More; accessed 15 September 2026.

=== FamilySearch record-hint collision: James McCaughan and Alexander McCaughan ===

The logged-in FamilySearch record search returned an indexed Ireland marriage result describing '''James Mc Caughan''' as father of '''Alexander Mc Caughan'''. The attached Family Tree match was '''MCGP-3S2''', but that profile is James McCaughan born about '''1827''', with spouse Catharine McConachie and children Alexander McCaughan ('''1847–1921''', 96QG-NVJ) and Robert Mc Caughan ('''1853–1934''', K4GP-RD8). The tree profile has no sources and the relationship was added in 2020.

This is a new and important exclusion. The attached tree person cannot be the older James proposed as Mary's father: he is too young, and his son Alexander was born decades after Mary's marriage and the 1837–1844 Glasgow baptisms. The indexed father statement may belong to a different McCaughan family or be an aggregation error; it must not be cited as evidence for Mary's parentage. Source: [[https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MCGP-3S2|FamilySearch tree profile MCGP-3S2]], and [[https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/record/results?count=100&q.givenName=James&q.surname=McCaughan&q.birthLikeDate.from=1760&q.birthLikeDate.to=1800&q.birthLikePlace=Antrim%2C%20Ireland|FamilySearch James McCaughan search results]], accessed 15 September 2026.

The same search also surfaced '''James McCaughan''' in the Irish Valuation Office Books for '''Shankill in 1838''' and '''Billy, Ballycastle in 1861'''. These are new locality leads, but the index does not expose enough detail to identify the tenant with [[McCaughan-68|McCaughan-68]], the Gortereghy tithe tenant, or Mary's father. The underlying valuation images should be checked for townland continuity, occupier changes and adjoining McCaughan households.
